name: Norton Commando
engine: 745 or 828 cc air-cooled OHV parallel twin, two Amal carbs, Isolastic mounts
intro: The Isolastic-mounted British twin. Isolastic shims and wet sumping are the two things to understand.

add.title: Check and shim the Isolastics
add.instructions: Check the front and rear Isolastic mounts for play. When shimming, keep the shims even on both sides.
add.reason: Worn or badly shimmed Isolastics make the bike handle badly and shake.

add.title: Check for wet sumping
add.instructions: Note the oil tank level when you park the bike and again a few days later. If a lot has drained into the sump, check the oil pump and timing cover seals.
add.reason: A worn pump can starve the top end of oil. Some wet sumping on a stored bike is normal.

H: Don't fit an anti-drain tap. Forgetting to open it can wreck the engine.

recallNote: Any recalls on bikes this old were closed long ago.

known.title: Wet sumping
known.what: Oil drains from the tank to the sump when the bike sits. It is common on dry-sump British twins.
